Summary: The FOMC kept the target range at 4.25%–4.50% and is continuing balance-sheet runoff, noting solid growth, low unemployment, and still-elevated inflation. However, the April 2025 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey points to headwinds: banks reported weaker demand (including for CRE), other and foreign banks tightened standards/terms for C&I loans while large banks kept C&I standards roughly unchanged, and lenders cited the economic outlook, supervisory/legislative changes, industry-specific problems, accounting standards, and lower risk tolerance. Tighter CRE lending and adjustments to credit lines reinforce ongoing stress in commercial real estate and softer financing needs. These SLOOS signals, together with Financial Stability Report vulnerabilities (elevated asset valuations, rising consumer delinquencies in some segments, run-prone short-term funding, and episodic Treasury market liquidity strains), argue for a more cautious tone than the baseline statement suggests. Policy implication: a patient “hold” bias with careful risk management, as tighter credit conditions could temper activity even as inflation remains above target.
